claude.country: Multinational (Human Dx online platform users worldwide)
claude.sample_unit: text-based medical case vignettes (40,762 physician differential diagnoses)

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of physicians alone, LLMs alone, and hybrid human-LLM collectives (top-k, MRR)
links.effect: Hybrid collectives outperformed single physicians, physician collectives, single LLMs and LLM ensembles; adding one LLM to physicians consistently increased performance; adding a physician raised all LLMs' accuracy. Simulated aggregation, not real users.
links.quote: Crucially, adding one LLM to the human diagnoses consistently increased performance for both individual physicians and human-only ensembles of different sizes, with the largest increase attained when adding the best-performing individual LLM or an all-LLM ensemble.

links.outcome: Comparison of LLM diagnostic accuracy against physicians on the same vignettes
links.effect: Four of five LLMs outperformed the average physician; the all-LLM ensemble strictly outperformed 85% of physicians and outperformed or tied with 93%.
links.quote: This percentage was highest for an LLM ensemble incorporating all five LLMs (i.e., strictly outperformed 85% of physicians and outperformed or tied with 93% of physicians).

links.outcome: Whether LLM differential diagnoses omitted the correct diagnosis
links.effect: LLMs did not list the correct diagnosis at all in 34% to 54% of cases depending on the LLM; individual physicians often supplied the missed diagnosis, frequently ranking it first.
links.quote: Crucially, when LLMs did not list the correct diagnosis at all (range across LLMs: 34% to 54%; Right -most columns), individual humans did mention it in a substantial number of cases (range across LLMs: 30% to 38%; Right -most columns excluding Bottom - Right cells), most frequently ranking it first (range across LLMs: 20% to 26%, Top - Right cells).

unlisted_practices: Aggregating multiple LLMs into ensembles to improve diagnostic accuracy
Hybrid human-LLM collective intelligence with performance-weighted majority voting for differential diagnosis

links.outcome: LLM diagnostic performance after adding physicians
links.effect: Adding a single physician increased performance for all LLMs; performance increased steadily with more humans.
links.quote: Adding a single physician increased performance for all LLMs even though individual physicians, on average, performed worse than most LLMs; and LLM performance increased steadily with adding more humans.

links.effect: Four of five LLMs outperformed the average physician; one did not.
links.quote: Comparing the individual LLM performance with that of the human users showed that four of the five LLMs outperformed the average physician.

links.outcome: Correct diagnosis missing from LLM top five
links.effect: LLMs did not list the correct diagnosis at all in 34% to 54% of cases.
links.quote: Crucially, when LLMs did not list the correct diagnosis at all (range across LLMs: 34% to 54%; Right -most columns), individual humans did mention it in a substantial number of cases (range across LLMs: 30% to 38%; Right -most columns excluding Bottom - Right cells), most frequently ranking it first (range across LLMs: 20% to 26%, Top - Right cells).

unlisted_practices: Weighted aggregation of physician and LLM differential diagnoses into hybrid collectives
Weighted ensembling of multiple LLM differential diagnoses

links.outcome: Diagnostic miss rates of stand-alone LLMs compared with physician diagnoses
links.effect: LLMs missed correct diagnosis in 34% to 54% of cases; individual physicians correctly identified the diagnosis in 30% to 38% of those cases (ranking it first in 20% to 26%).
links.quote: Crucially, when LLMs did not list the correct diagnosis at all (range across LLMs: 34% to 54%; Right -most columns), individual humans did mention it in a substantial number of cases (range across LLMs: 30% to 38%; Right -most columns excluding Bottom - Right cells), most frequently ranking it first (range across LLMs: 20% to 26%, Top - Right cells).

unlisted_practices: Hybrid collective intelligence combining physician and large language model differential diagnoses using weighted majority voting aggregation
Multi-LLM ensembling aggregating differential diagnoses across multiple large language models
